newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares end down in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares end down in dull trade.

text.p: Shanghai B shares ended Thursday down after a dull day of trade, with cash seen flowing into newly issued foreign-currency B shares, brokers said.
The B index fell 0.870 points or 0.97 percent to 89.206 on volume of 13.44 million shares worth $9.353 million.
Jinan Qingqi Motorcycle issued 230 million B shares late in May, and Heilongjiang Electric Power offered an additional 80 million shares on Wednesday.
Brokers said institutional investors put their money into these comparatively cheap but good value new B shares.
"Buying force on the secondary market has weakened as the new B shares are attracting a lot of capital," said one broker.
"The market is consolidating as shares with heavy index weighting are finding it difficult to rise beyond the current high levels without any new stimulus," another broker said.
"But there is strong support at low levels, indicating investors are still optimistic," he said.
Of 43 B shares, 42 traded with 27 down 10 flat and five up.
Shanghai Steel Tube Co was the biggest loser on speculative selling, slipping $0.014 or 8.53 percent to $0.150 on volume of 54,000 shares.

Pudong real estate counter Shanghai Jinqiao Export Processing Zone Development was the most actively traded on profit-taking, slipping $0.018 or 2.19 percent to $0.802 on volume of 1.3 million shares.
Shanghai's A share index was slightly down with investors sidelined amid on-going concern that Beijing could introduce more measures to cool the overheated market, brokers said.
The index edged down 0.639 points or 0.04 percent to 1,421.435 points on volume of 566.5 million shares worth 9.1 billion yuan.
But the SSE30 blue chip index bucked the market trend on institutional support, rising 13.475 points or 0.32 percent to 4,229.539 points.
Xiamen Xiaxin was the biggest loser on profit-taking, plunging 1.92 yuan or 9.97 percent to 17.33 yuan on volume of 1.5 million shares.
